answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may place bids or claim rewards. The protocol caps how much influence one bond earns, so splitting it among a thousand aliases gains no extra weight; if an identity double-spends a claim or violates an escrowed agreement, its bond is forfeited. This raises the attacker’s cost from cheap account creation to capital at risk and ties the penalty to provable misconduct. A reef oracle, a nadir price, or shale-based collateral can inform bond valuation, but none alone proves identity.
